boards.title: Your First Weekend at Furman University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A Friday-to-Sunday introduction to ten distinct Furman destinations, balancing student-life resources, campus landmarks, reflection, recreation, and nearby trail access.

cards.title: Friday: Find the Campus Crossroads
cards.subtitle: Begin inside Trone Student Center
cards.notes: Locate Student Life and Student Involvement, scan the meeting areas, and note a comfortable place where your group can reconnect later.
cards.short_summary: A practical first stop for learning where student organizations, campus services, seating, and dining converge.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman says Trone Student Center contains meeting and study space, student-organization offices, dining, student-life resources, and views of Furman Lake.
cards.access_notes: Published building hours vary by season; Furman says students may access Trone's commons spaces 24/7 by swiping a student ID.

cards.title: Friday: Meet the Bell Tower
cards.subtitle: Walk to the landmark beside Furman Lake
cards.notes: Use the tower as an easy group landmark, pause for the lakeside view, and take a photo while everyone is still together.
cards.short_summary: The lakeside tower supplies an unmistakable visual reference point for a first walk across campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman's current campus feature identifies the Bell Tower and Furman Lake together and documents the tower's clock chimes across the lake.
cards.source_title: 200 Things We Love About Furman - News
cards.access_notes: View from public campus paths; exercise ordinary care near the lake and do not enter restricted parts of the tower.

cards.title: Friday: Share the First Meal
cards.subtitle: Regroup at Daniel Dining Hall
cards.notes: Compare the available stations before choosing a meal, then use the table time to settle Saturday plans and exchange contact details.
cards.short_summary: A shared meal gives a new group time to turn introductions into a workable weekend plan.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman identifies Charles E. Daniel Dining Hall as an on-campus dining option with comfort foods and cuisines from around the world.
cards.source_title: Housing & Dining | Admissions & Aid | Furman University
cards.access_notes: Dining access, serving periods, and payment requirements may vary; consult Furman's current dining information before going.

cards.title: Saturday: Start Among the Roses
cards.subtitle: Take a quiet morning loop through the garden
cards.notes: Walk the paths at an unhurried pace, find the gazebo, and photograph the named garden without stepping into planting beds.
cards.short_summary: The named rose garden and gazebo offer a clearly defined outdoor start to Saturday's campus circuit.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman's current campus feature names the Rose Garden and gazebo, while a university news page identifies it as the Janie Earle Furman Rose Garden.
cards.source_title: Furman campus listed among 'most beautiful' - News
cards.access_notes: Use established outdoor paths and observe any temporary event, maintenance, or horticultural closures.

cards.title: Saturday: Learn the Library Layout
cards.subtitle: Identify a future study base
cards.notes: Find circulation, choose a study area you could recognize later, and note where to ask for research help before assignments begin.
cards.short_summary: An early orientation to the central library makes the next academic visit less improvisational.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman's 2025–26 campus map identifies James B. Duke Library as a 120,000-square-foot facility at the center of campus.
cards.access_notes: Library schedules change during breaks, holidays, and severe weather; verify the current Furman Libraries schedule before entering.

cards.title: Saturday: Pause at Vaughn Plaza
cards.subtitle: Add campus history to the route
cards.notes: Read the marker and examine the statue before discussing why this place of reflection sits beside the university library.
cards.short_summary: The plaza turns a walk between buildings into a specific encounter with Furman's institutional history.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman's current campus map says Joseph Vaughn Plaza was completed in 2021 and features a statue honoring Furman's first Black undergraduate student.
cards.access_notes: The plaza is a place of reflection; approach the statue and historical material respectfully and follow posted conditions.

cards.entity_name: Herman W. Lay Physical Activities Center
cards.title: Saturday: Scope Out the PAC
cards.subtitle: Learn where campus recreation happens
cards.notes: Bring your Furman ID, inspect the fitness and gathering areas, and check posted schedules before planning a later workout.
cards.short_summary: A short reconnaissance visit makes the campus recreation hub easier to use during the first full week.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman describes the Lay Physical Activities Center as its student-fitness and recreation hub, with exercise machines, a basketball court, studio, and study spaces.
cards.access_notes: A Furman or Campus Recreation and Wellness ID is required. Published hours vary among fall/spring, summer, breaks, and holidays.

cards.title: Sunday: Circle Furman Lake
cards.subtitle: Begin the day with a marked campus activity
cards.notes: Choose a comfortable pace, stay on the established walking trail, and use the loop to connect landmarks seen since Friday.
cards.short_summary: The documented lake trail links the weekend's separate stops into one coherent mental map of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman's 2026 campus feature specifically documents the Furman Lake walking trail as a named campus activity and place.
cards.source_title: 200 Things We Love About Furman - News
cards.access_notes: Use established paths, remain alert to weather and path conditions, and keep a safe distance from water and wildlife.

cards.title: Sunday: Visit the Place of Peace
cards.subtitle: Time the stop for weekend docent hours
cards.notes: Arrive during the published docent window, walk through the adjoining Asia Garden, and leave a few quiet minutes for reflection.
cards.short_summary: A documented weekend window makes this reconstructed Japanese structure a natural Sunday destination.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman says the Place of Peace was reconstructed from more than 2,400 pieces and lists public docents on Saturdays and Sundays from 1 to 3 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Published docent hours are Saturdays and Sundays, 1–3 p.m.; confirm the page before visiting because special closures may occur.

cards.title: Sunday: Follow the Trail Beyond Campus
cards.subtitle: Finish at Furman's Swamp Rabbit Trail access
cards.notes: Walk or ride only as far as your time and equipment allow, keep right, and set a turnaround point before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: The adjacent regional trail provides a straightforward final glimpse of Furman's connection to the surrounding community.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman's location page says students can bike or walk the Swamp Rabbit Trail directly from campus toward Travelers Rest or downtown Greenville.
cards.access_notes: This is a shared regional trail. Travel in daylight, follow posted trail rules, use suitable safety equipment, and turn back as conditions require.
